newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--light supply props up prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--light supply props up prices.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds drifted around unchanged in early afternoon trade on Monday as the lack of supply helped the market withstand the pressure of softer Treasury bonds, which dipped ahead of economic data.
"It's a typical, fairly quiet Monday in the municipal market, but the market is hanging right in there, the underlying tone is firm, there are no sellers," a trader said.
A key gauge of the secondary market, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, slipped to $944.3 million, a lean level, and one that shows dealers are not over-burdened with inventories.
Further, the new issuance market also was expected to be fairly subdued, as only around $2.507 billion in 122 sales were planned for the week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings, which totaled $1.780 billion in 47 sales, included a $350 million Los Angeles Unified School District offering through BancAmerica.

And a $300 million sale of revenue bonds by the New York State Metropolitan Transportation Authority was expected to help set the tone for New York City's offering next week of around $400 million of general obligation bonds and $100 million of Euronotes.
Another factor supporting municipal bonds was fairly large cash positions that institutions were believed to be holding. "There's still a lot of cash out there," a trader said.

These features left the municipal market mainly vulnerable to any surprisingly negative factors that might arise in this week's main economic data. These reports include retail sales for June on Tuesday, which were forcast at up 0.2 percent, according to a consensus poll of Reuters economists.
And on Wednesday, Consumer Prices for June were due out, also predicted to rise 0.2 percent.
In Chicago futures markets, September municipals eased one tick to 119-15/32, while September Treasury bonds shed eased three ticks to 114-1/32. The MOB spread steadied at 174.
In the secondary market, Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania & New Jersey Revenues, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 100, down one eighth.
And Jefferson County, Alabama Sewer Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, wre bid at 102, against 5.50 percent, NET, on Friday.
